# Belinda

## Overview

- **Age:** Fourteen years old (as of Volume 2)  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>
- **Origin:** St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010)</sub>
- **Role:** Handmaiden and domestic servant  <sub>[v2 c28 P18](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0018), [v2 c28 P56](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0056)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Belinda the Fourth  <sub>[v2 c21 P61](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0061), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>; Leonora  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042)</sub>

## Appearance

Belinda has freckles on her face, a snub nose, and a wide mouth with broad smiles. In her youth, she frequently wore large, bright blue bows that fluttered during her daily activities. As she grew into a young woman, she stopped wearing the blue ribbons and adopted a massive pompadour hairstyle.

_Sources: [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011), [v3 c23 P7](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0007), [v4 c3 P37](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0037)_

## Personality

Belinda is energetic, joyful, and deeply devoted to her mistress. She possesses a welcoming nature and displays complete obedience to Miss Rosalind's desires, regardless of how foolish others might view them. She enjoys food and takes pride in her friendships, though she can feel indignant when excluded from secrets.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P61](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0061), [v2 c21 P73](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0073), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c23 P3](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0003), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029), [v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048), [v2 c28 P56](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0056), [v2 c30 P11](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0011)_

## History

Belinda was born Leonora Bowman, the youngest of Mrs. Bowman's daughters. Following the path of her older sisters, she came to live at Echo Cottage with Miss Rosalind at age fourteen as a domestic helper in exchange for room, board, and clothing. Because Miss Rosalind routinely addressed her domestic helpers by the name of the original handmaiden, Leonora was dubbed "Belinda the Fourth." She diligently served Miss Rosalind, cooked, helped make clothing, and assisted with preparations for events. After turning sixteen, she spent time living in Boston with Miss Rosalind and her new husband, though she suffered from intense homesickness and expressed a deep preference for St. Brendan's Island. Later, she married a bricklayer named Tom. She returned to attend Nell Harcourt's wedding, where she happily helped throw rice and shoes to wish the bride good fortune.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c28 P18](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0018), [v2 c30 P3](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0003), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v3 c23 P1](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0001), [v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010), [v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042), [v4 c4 P16](../source/v04-c04.md#nw-v04-c04-p0016)_

## Quotes

> Please, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, it can easily be noticed that a secret exists between you and Miss Rosalind, and I believe, asking for your forgiveness if I am being overly bold, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, that withholding it from me is truly unkind, considering how close we have all been as friends.  <sub>[v2 c28 P48](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0048)</sub>

> I’m truly happy about that. People at home claimed I had one, though I figured they probably merely wished to annoy me. A Yankee accent is something I don't desire. I have nothing at all against the Yankees, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. They are genuinely civilized. However, I would choose old St. Brendan’s Island over them any day.  <sub>[v3 c23 P10](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0010)</sub>

> Gracious, no, Miss Harcourt, ma’am. I would not have any idea who he was referring to if he did. Naturally, at the time we were wed he was required to recite, 'I take thee, Leonora,’ and I swear to you, Miss Harcourt, ma’am, I have carried the most terrible impression ever since that he was not speaking to me and I have not been properly wedded whatsoever. And thus you are about to be wedded your own self, Miss Harcourt, ma’am? I ever imagined I should enjoy being wed to a physician. It would be exceedingly useful whenever the little ones contracted measles and croup. Tom is merely a bricklayer, yet he possesses a truly fine disposition. When I remarked to him, says I, 'Tom, may I attend Miss Harcourt’s wedding? I intend to go regardless, yet I should prefer to possess your permission,’ he simply responds, 'Suit yourself, Belinda, and you’ll suit me.’ That is a truly agreeable sort of spouse to possess, Miss Harcourt, ma’am.  <sub>[v4 c3 P42](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0042)</sub>
